evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God gave David the Psalms (Zabur) (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in The last words of David: A just ruler is like the morning sun on a cloudless day; Poem opening with 'Oracle (ne'um) of the man...' formula; The spirit of God speaks through the king's tongue; The wicked are thorns that cannot be handled and are burned; God has made an everlasting covenant with the king's house.

Only in David's census, the plague, and Araunah's threshing floor: Itinerary of census-takers around the land's borders; The king's heart strikes him after a sin; God halts the destroying angel at a specific spot: 'Enough, stay your hand'; The commander objects to the king's census; Counting the people requires a ransom for each life to avert plague; God himself incites a person to an evil act; The believers' pride in their great numbers avails nothing and the earth grows narrow for them (Hunayn); Census totals given tribe by tribe.

title: Nathan's oracle of the eternal house of David and David's prayer ↔ Nathan's oracle of an eternal house and David's prayer
summary: 9 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The king's son, not the king, will build the house for God's name (weight 6.7); God promises to make the chosen one's name great (weight 6.7); Israel is the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem for himself (weight 6.7); Prayer of humility: 'Who am I and what is my house?' (weight 6.7); God has never dwelt in a house but moved from tent to tent (weight 6.7); A prophet approves a plan, then is corrected by a revelation that night (weight 6.7); God took the ruler from following the sheep (weight 6.7); God declares the king his son: 'I will be his father and he my son' (weight 6.0); God promises David's house and throne will endure forever (weight 5.8). Pair score 58.6.

Only in Nathan's oracle of the eternal house of David and David's prayer: God's steadfast love will not be withdrawn from the heir as it was from the previous king; The king, living in a cedar palace, proposes to build a house for God; Obscure phrase 'this is the torah of man (adam)'; Wordplay on 'house' as temple and as dynasty; God disciplines Israel as a man disciplines his son; Whether God has, begets or takes sons or other offspring [contrast between the texts]; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts]; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'.

Only in Nathan's oracle of an eternal house and David's prayer: Pun on 'house': the king would build God a house; God will build the king a house (dynasty); Revelation described as God 'uncovering the ear' of his servant; The king lives in a cedar house while the ark of God remains under curtains; 'There is none like you and no God beside you'; Chronicles differs in a specific detail from its parallel in Samuel–Kings.

Only in Nebuchadnezzar demands his dream be told; the mystery revealed to Daniel: The magicians say only the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh, could reveal such a thing; The king demands that his experts tell him the dream itself as well as its meaning, on pain of death; God knows what is in darkness and light dwells with him; A hidden mystery (raz) is revealed to the seer in a night vision; The enraged king orders all the wise men of the capital killed; Threat that offenders will be torn limb from limb and their houses made a dunghill; Courtiers address the ruler 'O king, live forever'; The king's experts cannot interpret the dream.

Only in Owner of sovereignty: On the day each soul finds what good and evil it did present before it, wishing a far distance from its evil; Believers may not take unbelievers as allies, unless guarding against them (tuqat); God warns you of himself (yuhadhdhirukum allahu nafsahu); God makes night enter day and day night, brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living; O God, owner of sovereignty, you give it to whom you will and take it from whom you will; you exalt and abase; God gives justice to the poor and seats kings (or the lowly) on the throne; The Most High rules the kingdom of men, gives it to whom he wills and sets over it the lowliest of men; God provides for whom he wills without reckoning (bi-ghayri hisab); Hymn of reversals: the barren bears seven, the mighty broken, the poor raised from the dung-heap.

Only in The statue of four metals and the stone cut without hands: Destroyed kingdoms become like chaff from the summer threshing floors carried away by the wind; There is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries (gale razin) and makes known what will be at the end of days; A foreign king confesses Israel's God as 'God of gods and Lord of kings, revealer of mysteries'; Iron mixed with clay signifies kingdoms mingling by intermarriage ('the seed of men') yet not holding together; The pagan king falls on his face before the Jewish seer and orders offerings and incense for him; Successive kingdoms or ages symbolized by declining metals (gold, silver, bronze, iron); Dream of a great statue with head of gold, chest of silver, belly of bronze, legs of iron and feet of iron mixed with clay; A stone cut out without hands strikes the statue and becomes a great mountain filling the earth; A sequence of four world kingdoms (or ages), each inferior or more violent than the last; Persian ruler styled 'king of kings'; 'Your kingdom is a kingdom of all ages and your dominion through all generations'.

title: Passover, Weeks, Booths; judges; no Asherah ↔ Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice
summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy (weight 6.7); Who must make pilgrimage to the sanctuary, and how often [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Three annual pilgrimage festivals when every male appears before God (weight 5.3). Pair score 18.3.

Only in Passover, Weeks, Booths; judges; no Asherah: Unleavened bread, bread of affliction, because you left Egypt in haste; Justice, justice shall you pursue; No Asherah tree planted beside God's altar and no standing stone; Passover in the month of Aviv, at evening, at the chosen place; Feast of Weeks counted seven weeks from the first sickle in the standing grain; Seven full weeks (fifty days) counted from the sheaf offering to the new grain offering; Appoint judges and officers in every town to judge righteously; Passover offering boiled (bishalta) and eaten, flock or herd; Rejoice before God with sons, daughters, slaves and the Levite; Feast of Booths seven days after gathering threshing floor and winepress; you shall be only joyful; What is slaughtered on stone altars (nuṣub/anṣāb) is forbidden; the stones are abomination; Seven-day festival of dwelling in booths recalling the wilderness; and 3 more.

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts]; A place recognized as the house of God and gate of heaven; Who chose or founded the single sanctuary of sacrifice, and when [divergence between the texts]; and 4 more.

title: Idolater's trial; witnesses; high court; law of the king ↔ The debt verse
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: How many witnesses are required [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); No one put to death on the testimony of a single witness (weight 5.4). Pair score 11.4.

Only in Idolater's trial; witnesses; high court; law of the king: King writes a copy of the Torah and reads it all his days; King must be chosen by God from among brothers, not a foreigner; Hand of the witnesses first against the condemned, then the people's; Who, if anyone, inherits Egypt's land after the exodus [divergence between the texts]; Limits on how many wives the leader may take [divergence between the texts]; Made attractive to men: women, sons, heaped-up gold and silver, branded horses, cattle and tillage; Difficult cases referred to the Levitical priests and judge at the chosen place; defiance is capital; Amassing war horses, and trust in God [contrast between the texts]; Blemished animal (lame, blind) may not be sacrificed; Formula: you shall purge the evil from your midst; Prohibition of worshipping sun, moon, stars, the host of heaven; King must not multiply horses, wives or silver and gold, nor return the people to Egypt.

Only in The debt verse: A debt for a fixed term must be written by a just scribe, dictated by the debtor or his guardian; Two male witnesses, or one man and two women so that if one errs the other reminds her; On a journey without a scribe a pledge in hand (rihan maqbuda) is taken; A land deed made in a sealed copy and an open copy, witnessed and the silver weighed; A witness who hears a public adjuration and withholds testimony bears guilt.

Q: first an enumerated permission (innā aḥlalnā laka azwājaka ... khāliṣatan laka min dūni l-muʾminīn), then a freeze: lā yaḥillu laka n-nisāʾu min baʿdu wa-lā an tabaddala bihinna min azwājin wa-law aʿjabaka ḥusnuhunna. sides.note: The prophet who forges a message falls under God's sanction: ʾaḵ han-nāḇîʾ ʾăšer yāzîḏ lə-ḏabbēr dāḇār bi-šmî ʾēṯ ʾăšer lōʾ ṣiwwîṯîw ... û-mēṯ han-nāḇîʾ hahûʾ vs. am yaqūlūna ftarāhu qul ini ftaraytuhu fa-lā tamlikūna lī mina llāhi shayʾan. Deuteronomy gives the community a rule to judge the prophet; the Prophet turns the rule round as his own defence: if he forged it, God would deal with him, and no one could save him.

matches.label: False witness receives the punishment he plotted for his brother
matches.note: fa-jlidūhum thamānīna jaldatan wa-lā taqbalū lahum shahādatan abadan ~ wə-hinnēh ʿēd šeqer ... wa-ʿăśîtem lô kaʾăšer zāmam laʿăśôt lə-ʾāḥîw: the false accuser is punished. Deut gives him the penalty he intended (talion); the Quran sets a fixed flogging, disqualifies him as a witness, and leaves room for repentance (illā lladhīna tābū, 24:5).

matches.label: Who is exempted from going out to war
matches.note: Who may stay home from the campaign. Deuteronomy exempts by circumstance of property and family: mî hā-ʾîš ʾăšer bānâ ḇayiṯ ḥāḏāš ... nāṭaʿ kerem ... ʾēraś ʾiššâ wə-lōʾ ləqāḥāh yēlēḵ wə-yāšōḇ lə-ḇêṯô. The Quran rejects exactly that excuse: sa-yaqūlu laka l-mukhallafūna mina l-aʿrābi shaghalatnā amwālunā wa-ahlūnā (our property and families kept us busy), and exempts by disability only: laysa ʿalā l-aʿmā ḥarajun wa-lā ʿalā l-aʿraji ḥarajun wa-lā ʿalā l-marīḍi ḥaraj.

matches.label: Whether the enemy's trees may be cut down in a siege
matches.note: Cutting the enemy's trees during a siege: opposite rulings. Deuteronomy: kî ṯāṣûr ʾel ʿîr ... lōʾ ṯašḥîṯ ʾeṯ ʿēṣāh ... kî mimmennû ṯōʾḵēl, only non-fruit trees may be cut (raq ʿēṣ ʾăšer tēḏaʿ kî lōʾ ʿēṣ maʾăḵāl hûʾ). Quran: mā qaṭaʿtum min līnatin aw taraktumūhā qāʾimatan ʿalā uṣūlihā fa-bi-idhni llāhi wa-li-yukhziya l-fāsiqīn (whatever palms you cut or left standing was by God's leave). matches.note: Deut 24:1 kî māṣāʾ bāh ʿerwat dābār wĕ-kātab lāh sēper kĕrîtut wĕ-nātan bĕ-yādāh wĕ-šillĕḥāh: divorce for 'some indecency', by a written bill handed to her; Q 2:228-229 wa-l-muṭallaqātu yatarabbaṣna bi-anfusihinna thalāthata qurūʾin ... aṭ-ṭalāqu marratāni fa-imsākun bi-maʿrūfin aw tasrīḥun bi-iḥsān: no grounds and no document named; a waiting period of three menstrual cycles, the husband's right to take her back within it, and a limit of two revocable divorces. šillaḥ / sarraḥa, both 'send away'.

passages.text: כִּֽי יִקַּ֥ח אִ֛ישׁ אִשָּׁ֖ה וּבְעָלָ֑הּ וְהָיָ֞ה אִם לֹ֧א תִמְצָא חֵ֣ן בְּעֵינָ֗יו כִּי מָ֤צָא בָהּ֙ עֶרְוַ֣ת דָּבָ֔ר וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּיתֽוֹ

وَٱلْمُطَلَّقَٰتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ ثَلَٰثَةَ قُرُوٓءٍ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ إِنْ أَرَادُوٓا۟ إِصْلَٰحًا وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ

ٱلطَّلَٰقُ مَرَّتَانِ فَإِمْسَاكٌۢ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌۢ بِإِحْسَٰنٍ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَأْخُذُوا۟ مِمَّآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْـًٔا إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِۦ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ

matches.label: Whether a divorced wife may return to her first husband after another marriage
matches.note: Opposite rulings on the same case. Deut 24:4 lōʾ yûkal baʿlāh hā-rīšôn ʾăšer šillĕḥāh lāšûb lĕ-qaḥtāh ... ʾaḥărê ʾăšer huṭṭammāʾâ kî tôʿēbâ hîʾ: after she has been another man's wife the first husband may never take her back, it is an abomination; Q 2:230 fa-in ṭallaqahā fa-lā taḥillu lahu min baʿdu ḥattā tankiḥa zawjan ghayrahu fa-in ṭallaqahā fa-lā junāḥa ʿalayhimā an yatarājaʿā: after the third divorce she may return to the first husband only after marrying another. The intervening marriage that bars return in Deut is the condition for return in the Quran.

matches.note: Grounds and house reversed. Deut 24:1 kî māṣāʾ vāh ʿerwat dāvār we-kātav lāh sēfer kerîtut ... we-šillḥāh mi-bbêtô (he finds 'some indecency', writes a writ, sends her out of HIS house). sides.note: The same sequence: no other god, no killing, no adultery, no false witness: lā yadʿūna maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhara wa-lā yaqtulūna n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi wa-lā yaznūna ... lā yashhadūna z-zūra ~ lōʾ yihyeh ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāf ... lōʾ taʿăneh və-rēʿăkā ʿēd šāqer. Changes: the absolute lōʾ tirṣāḥ gets an exception ('except by right', illā bi-l-ḥaqq); theft is left out; the commands become a description of the righteous (alladhīna lā ...), followed by doubled punishment and an exception for those who repent (25:69-70).

Exodus: lōʾ yihyeh ləḵā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāp̄ lōʾ tiḡnōḇ lōʾ ṯaʿăneh ḇə-rēʿăḵā ʿēḏ šāqer. title: Bureaucratic oppression, the love of money and wealth that perishes ↔ Rivalry, time and the slanderer

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Riches kept by their owner to his hurt, lost in a bad venture, so that his son has nothing in hand (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Bureaucratic oppression, the love of money and wealth that perishes: He will not much remember the days of his life because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart; When goods increase, those who eat them increase; the owner only sees them with his eyes; The profit of the land is for all; a king is for (served by) the cultivated field; Sweet is the sleep of the laborer whether he eats little or much, but the surfeit of the rich will not let him sleep; He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance with income; If you see oppression of the poor in a province, do not be amazed: a high one watches over a high one, and higher ones over them; 'Naked I came from my mother's womb and naked I shall return there'; What profit (yitron) has a man from all his toil under the sun?; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

Only in Rivalry, time and the slanderer: Knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin) and the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin): you will see hell; God's kindled fire rises over the hearts and is closed over them in extended columns; Oath by time or the afternoon (al-'asr): humankind is in loss; Rivalry in piling up (al-takathur) distracts people until they visit the graves; they will be asked about the pleasures; A fire is closed over the damned (mu'sada); Hell given proper names: Laza (scalp-stripper), Saqar (scorcher, leaves nothing), al-Hutama (the crusher), Hawiya (the abyss); Do not go about as a talebearer among your people; Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal; Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' (wa ma adraka ma) introducing an eschatological term.

title: Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing) ↔ Those who stayed behind, the exempt, and the Bedouin

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Let them laugh a little and weep much (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing): Do not be quick to anger, for anger lodges in the bosom of fools; Do not say 'Why were the former days better than these?', for it is not from wisdom you ask this; The end of a thing is better than its beginning; patience is better than pride; Like the crackling of thorns (sirim) under a pot (sir), so is the laughter of the fool; In the day of prosperity be joyful, in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other; A good name is better than good oil (shem / shemen), and the day of death than the day of birth; Better to go to the house of mourning than to the house of feasting, for that is the end of all men; the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; Oppression makes a wise man foolish and a bribe destroys the heart; Vexation is better than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made glad; Consider the work of God: who can make straight what he has made crooked?; Wisdom is a shelter (shade) as money is a shelter; wisdom gives life to its possessor; A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, favor rather than silver and gold; and 1 more.

Only in Those who stayed behind, the exempt, and the Bedouin: The Bedouin (al-a'rab) are harder in unbelief and hypocrisy; Shirkers say 'do not go out in the heat'; hell's fire is hotter; Poor volunteers turn away weeping because the prophet has no mounts for them; Who is excused from going out to war [divergence between the texts]; Even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of joy is grief; The prophet must never pray over a dead hypocrite or stand at his grave; Catalogue of believers: repenting, worshiping, praising, wandering/fasting (sa'ihun), bowing, prostrating, enjoining right; God uses the unbelievers' wealth and children to punish them in this life; Hypocrites swear excuses and ask permission to stay behind from the campaign; Exemptions from war for a new house, unharvested vineyard, betrothed bride, or faintheartedness; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear.

title: Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution ↔ The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: When the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, God is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back! (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution: Because sentence (pitgam) against an evil deed is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil; There are righteous men who receive what the wicked deserve and wicked who receive what the righteous deserve; No man has power over the wind (ruah) to restrain it, nor power over the day of death; there is no discharge in war; Keep the king's command because of the oath of God; who can say to him 'What are you doing?'; I saw the wicked buried with honor, going in and out of the holy place, and praised in the city where they did such things; Who is like the wise and knows the interpretation (pesher) of a thing? Wisdom makes his face shine; Man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun; even if the wise man claims to know, he cannot find it; For everything there is a season and a time for every matter under heaven (birth and death, planting and uprooting, etc.); Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; Wisdom or the fear of YHWH adds days and years of life; the years of the wicked are shortened; Human days on earth are a shadow; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

Only in The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat: The damned eat of Zaqqum to fill their bellies and drink boiling water like thirst-crazed camels (al-him); A noble Quran in a hidden Book which none touch but the purified; The 'hospitality' (nuzul) of the deniers is boiling water and roasting in hell; The damned had lived in luxury and persisted in the great sin (al-hinth al-'azim); 'I swear by the positions (setting-places) of the stars, a mighty oath if you knew'; Have you seen the water you drink? Did you send it down from the rain-clouds? We could make it bitter (ujaj); For those brought near: rest (rawh), fragrance (rayhan) and a garden of bliss; The Companions of the Left are in scorching wind (samum), boiling water and the shade of black smoke (yahmum), neither cool nor kind; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; Fire kindled from a tree that God made grow [divergence between the texts]; The scripture exists with God in the 'Mother of the Book' (umm al-kitab), a heavenly archetype; and 8 more.

title: Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city ↔ Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city: Man does not know his time; like fish caught in a net and birds in a snare, people are trapped in an evil time; A great king besieges a small city; a poor wise man delivers it by his wisdom, yet no one remembers him; The race is not to the swift nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise; time and chance (pega') happen to all; Wisdom is better than might and weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good; A wise man scales the city of the mighty and brings down its trusted stronghold; 'Better is X than Y' comparative saying (tov ... min).

Only in Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book: God's book speaks against them with truth: 'We used to have transcribed (nastansikh) all that you did'; What God's heavenly book records: names or deeds [divergence between the texts]; Deniers of resurrection say there is only our first death and challenge the prophet to bring back their fathers; To God belongs the grandeur (kibriya') in the heavens and the earth; Whether death is the end: asked, held by sceptics, or answered by resurrection [response between the texts]; On the day of the Hour every community is seen kneeling (jathiya), each called to its book of deeds; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; The prophet's mission and the hearers' closed ears, eyes and hearts: caused, sealed, or beyond his cure [divergence between the texts]; God forgets the damned today as they forgot the meeting of this day; Do evildoers think God will make them equal to the righteous in life and in death?; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; and 2 more.

title: Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The queen consults her chiefs, who defer to her; she observes that kings who enter a town ruin it and humble its nobles (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal: Royal decree that every man shall rule in his own house; Merry with wine, the king orders the queen brought in her crown to show her beauty to his guests; A decree written into the laws of Persia and Media cannot be revoked; At the royal banquet drinking is by rule, no one compelled; The disobedient queen is deposed and her royalty given to 'another better than she'; The queen refuses to come at the king's command and the king is enraged; King holds a banquet showing his riches for 180 days; The queen holds a separate banquet for the women; Seven named eunuchs serve the king; Palace garden decorated with fine hangings, marble columns, gold and silver couches and mosaic pavement; Susa the citadel (Shushan ha-birah) as setting; Royal decree sent to each province in its own script and each people in its own language; and 2 more.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 22 more.

title: The search for virgins, Esther made queen, and Mordecai foils the eunuchs' plot ↔ Two hearts, zihar, adopted sons, and the prophet's wives as mothers
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether an adopted or fostered child counts as one's own child [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in The search for virgins, Esther made queen, and Mordecai foils the eunuchs' plot: King grants the provinces a remission and gives gifts at the new queen's feast; Virgins gathered from all provinces so the king may choose a new queen; Hero's genealogy runs back to Kish the Benjaminite (Saul's father); Heroine at the foreign court hides her people and kindred on her guardian's orders; Convicted plotters against the king are hanged (impaled) on a tree; A courtier's service is recorded in the royal book of chronicles before the king; Heroine has a Hebrew name (Hadassah) and a foreign one (Esther); Two eunuch doorkeepers plot to kill the king; the hero learns of it and reports it; A royal eunuch keeps the harem and supplies the women's cosmetics; Hero's family was deported from Jerusalem with King Jeconiah; Heroine wins the favor of her guardian official, who gives her special treatment; Heroine asks for nothing beyond what the eunuch advises when she goes to the king; and 5 more.

Only in Two hearts, zihar, adopted sons, and the prophet's wives as mothers: God took a solemn covenant (mithaq) from the prophets: Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus son of Mary; Adopted sons are not one's sons; call them by their fathers' names, or as brothers in religion and clients; God has not put two hearts inside any man; Blood relatives are nearer to one another (in inheritance) in God's book; The prophet's wives are the mothers of the believers and may not be married after him; Zihar: a husband declaring his wife 'like my mother's back'; she is not his mother, the saying is false and abhorrent.

The Quran forbids treating the fosterling as a child (mā jaʿala adʿiyāʾakum abnāʾakum) but requires the same naming practice, udʿūhum li-ābāʾihim. The fosterling as 'daughter' is the point of contrast; 2:15 is the point of agreement.

title: The pursuit and the parting of the sea ↔ Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith
summary: 4 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed, 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows (weight 6.7); Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites (weight 6.7); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 29.2.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Only in Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith: Only some youths (dhurriyya) of Moses' people believed him, fearing Pharaoh; As he drowns Pharaoh declares faith in the God of the Israelites, too late; Pharaoh's body is saved from the sea to be a sign for those after him; Moses prays God to obliterate Pharaoh's wealth and harden their hearts so they do not believe until they see punishment; Moses and Aaron are told to make their people's houses in Egypt a qibla (place/direction of prayer); God's instruction about the Israelites' houses in Egypt before the exodus [divergence between the texts]; Threatened believers say 'to our Lord we return' and pray for patience and to die as muslims; Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows [divergence between the texts]; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes; How Moses' own people in Egypt respond to his message [divergence between the texts]; The king confesses he has sinned and that God is righteous; Who causes Pharaoh's refusal: God hardening his heart, or Pharaoh and his people themselves; and 6 more.

matches.note: Motive for the pursuit: Exodus gives Pharaoh's regret (mah zōʾt ʿāśînû kî šillaḥnû ʾet Yiśrāʾēl mēʿovdēnû) and God hardening his heart so he will pursue and God be glorified (wə-ḥizzaqtî ʾet lēv Parʿōh wə-rādaf ʾaḥărêhem wə-ʾikkāvədâ bə-Farʿōh); Q 26:52 says only that God warned Moses 'innakum muttabaʿūn', and 26:54-55 gives Pharaoh's contempt (la-shirdhimatun qalīlūna ... la-ghāʾiẓūn). There is no regret over losing slaves and no hardening.

passages.text: וְחִזַּקְתִּ֣י אֶת לֵב פַּרְעֹה֮ וְרָדַ֣ף אַחֲרֵיהֶם֒ וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל חֵיל֔וֹ וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵֽן

matches.note: Ending of the sea story: Exod 14:31 wa-yyîrəʾû hā-ʿām ʾet YHWH wa-yyaʾămînû ba-YHWH û-və-Mōše ʿavdô, the people believe, and the Song follows (15:1). The Quran's refrain: inna fī dhālika la-āyatan wa-mā kāna aktharuhum muʾminīna, a sign, yet most of them did not believe. Faith at the sea becomes unbelief despite the sign, aimed at the Quran's own audience.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; and 20 more.

Only in Midian, Ad, Thamud, Korah, Pharaoh and Haman punished: The prophet Shu'ayb is sent to his kin, the people of Midian (Madyan); List of punishment types for the nations: stone-storm, the Shout, swallowing by the earth, drowning; How the people of Midian came to be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; God did not wrong them; they wronged themselves (refrain); Korah (Qarun), Pharaoh and Haman are grouped as arrogant opponents of Moses; Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings; God casts great hailstones from heaven, killing more than the sword; List of destroyed peoples or hosts (e.g. 'Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh) recalled as warning; The earth opens its mouth and swallows rebels alive into Sheol.

matches.note: What Moses does to the sea after crossing. Exodus: wa-yēṭ mōšeh ʾeṯ yāḏô ʿal hay-yām ... wə-yāšuḇû ham-mayim ʿal miṣrayim (he stretches out his hand again to bring the waters back). matches.label: Moses helps the women at the water of Midian
matches.note: At the water of Midian: Exodus has seven daughters of the priest of Midian (šebaʿ bānôt) who draw water, shepherds who drive them off (wa-ygārəšûm), and Moses who rescues them (wa-yyôšiʿān) and waters their flock. The Quran has two women holding back their flock (imraʾatayni tadhūdāni) until the shepherds finish, explaining abūnā shaykhun kabīrun; Moses waters for them unasked, then withdraws to the shade and prays (rabbi innī limā anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqīr). There is no fight with the shepherds.

فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ

matches.label: Moses' father-in-law in Midian

title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry ↔ Moses kills the Egyptian, is warned, and flees toward Midian
summary: 5 correspondences read side by side: 4 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How Moses killed the Egyptian [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The retort Moses hears on the day after the killing [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand (weight 6.7); How Moses learns that his life is sought [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Kinsman rebuffs the hero: 'Who made you prince and judge over us?' (weight 6.7); How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Hero flees the king's death sentence to a foreign land (weight 5.8). Pair score 45.5.

Only in Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry: The foundling's weeping moves the finder to compassion; The hero's parents are introduced anonymously as a Levite man and a Levite woman; Mother sees that her newborn 'is good' (ki tov); Hero names his son for being a stranger in a foreign land; Infant adopted by a royal woman [divergence between the texts]; The groaning of the oppressed rises to God, who hears and remembers his covenant; Hero drives off shepherds and waters the flock of women at a well; What the Midianite daughters do after Moses helps them [divergence between the texts]; Moses helps the women at the water of Midian [divergence between the texts]; Moses' father-in-law in Midian [divergence between the texts]; Moses killed a man and God delivered him from distress, then tried him with trials [divergence between the texts]; Who decides that Moses be put on the water [divergence between the texts]; and 19 more.

Only in Moses kills the Egyptian, is warned, and flees toward Midian: Moses calls his killing 'the work of Satan' and asks forgiveness, which is granted; A man comes running from the far end of the city to warn the hero that the chiefs plot to kill him; When Moses reached his full strength God gave him judgment and knowledge; Moses killed a man and God delivered him from distress, then tried him with trials.

Moses kills the Egyptian, is warned, and flees toward Midian

matches.label: How Moses killed the Egyptian
matches.note: The killing: Exodus has Moses see an Egyptian beating a Hebrew 'of his brothers', look this way and that and see no one (wa-yyifen kōh wā-khōh wa-yyarʾ kî ʾên ʾîš), strike him and hide him in the sand. The Quran has him find two men fighting, one of his party (shīʿa) and one of his enemy; at his kinsman's cry for help he strikes one blow and the man dies (fa-wakazahu Mūsā fa-qaḍā ʿalayhi). There is no looking around and no hiding of the body; the act is unpremeditated.

passages.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם וַיִּגְדַּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֶל אֶחָ֔יו וַיַּ֖רְא בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מַכֶּ֥ה אִישׁ עִבְרִ֖י מֵאֶחָֽיו
וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל

وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ مُّضِلٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged
matches.note: Moral verdict on the killing: Exodus passes none; Moses only fears exposure (wa-yyîrāʾ Mōše wa-yyōʾmar ʾākhēn nôdaʿ had-dāvār). The Quran has Moses judge it at once, hādhā min ʿamali sh-shayṭān ... rabbi innī ẓalamtu nafsī fa-ghfir lī, and God forgives him (fa-ghafara lahu), so Moses is a repentant penitent before he is a prophet.

passages.text: וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל
וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ הַלְהָרְגֵ֨נִי֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֑י וַיִּירָ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע הַדָּבָֽר

وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ مُّضِلٌّ مُّبِينٌ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى فَٱغْفِرْ لِى فَغَفَرَ لَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيرًا لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ

matches.label: The retort Moses hears on the day after the killing
matches.note: The second day: in Exodus two Hebrews (šənê ʾănāšîm ʿIvrîm) fight, Moses rebukes the guilty one, and that Hebrew retorts mî śāməkhā lə-ʾîš śar wə-šōfēṭ ʿālênû ha-lə-hārəgēnî ʾattâ ʾōmēr ka-ʾăšer hāragtā ʾet ham-Miṣrî. In the Quran the same kinsman again calls for help against an enemy, Moses calls the kinsman 'clearly misguided' (la-ghawiyyun mubīn), and as he moves to strike the enemy he hears a-turīdu an taqtulanī kamā qatalta nafsan bi-l-amsi in turīdu illā an takūna jabbāran fī l-arḍ. 'Prince and judge' becomes 'tyrant' (jabbār).

passages.text: וַיֵּצֵא֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהִנֵּ֛ה שְׁנֵֽי אֲנָשִׁ֥ים עִבְרִ֖ים נִצִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לָֽרָשָׁ֔ע לָ֥מָּה תַכֶּ֖ה רֵעֶֽךָ
וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ הַלְהָרְגֵ֨נִי֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֑י וַיִּירָ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע הַדָּבָֽר
فَأَصْبَحَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَنصَرَهُۥ بِٱلْأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُۥ قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّكَ لَغَوِىٌّ مُّبِينٌ

فَلَمَّآ أَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَبْطِشَ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ عَدُوٌّ لَّهُمَا قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِى كَمَا قَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۢا بِٱلْأَمْسِ إِن تُرِيدُ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ

matches.label: How Moses learns that his life is sought
matches.note: How the danger reaches Moses: Exodus has wa-yyišmaʿ Parʿōh ʾet had-dāvār haz-zeh wa-yvaqqēš lahărōg ʾet Mōše, Pharaoh himself; the Quran has the chiefs plotting (al-malaʾa yaʾtamirūna bika li-yaqtulūka) and an unnamed sympathizer running from the far end of the city to warn him (wa-jāʾa rajulun min aqṣā l-madīnati yasʿā).

passages.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לַהֲרֹ֣ג אֶת מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּבְרַ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ מִדְיָ֖ן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עַֽל הַבְּאֵֽר
وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌ مِّنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ فَٱخْرُجْ إِنِّى لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ הַלְהָרְגֵ֨נִי֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֑י וַיִּירָ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע הַדָּבָֽר

فَلَمَّآ أَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَبْطِشَ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ عَدُوٌّ لَّهُمَا قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِى كَمَا قَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۢا بِٱلْأَمْسِ إِن تُرِيدُ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ

title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry ↔ Pharaoh's oppression and the infant Moses on the water
summary: 6 correspondences read side by side: 5 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Sister offers to find a nurse [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Who decides that Moses be put on the water [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Infant returned to his own mother to nurse [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Infant adopted by a royal woman [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Infant placed in a container and set on the water [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Infant's sister watches over him (weight 6.0); Infant adopted by a royal woman (weight 6.0); Sister offers to find a nurse (weight 5.8); Infant returned to his own mother to nurse (weight 5.8); Infant found by members of a royal household (weight 5.6); Infant placed in a container and set on the water (weight 5.6). Pair score 67.8.

Only in Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry: The foundling's weeping moves the finder to compassion; The hero's parents are introduced anonymously as a Levite man and a Levite woman; Mother sees that her newborn 'is good' (ki tov); Hero names his son for being a stranger in a foreign land; The groaning of the oppressed rises to God, who hears and remembers his covenant; Hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand; Hero drives off shepherds and waters the flock of women at a well; How Moses learns that his life is sought [divergence between the texts]; How Moses killed the Egyptian [divergence between the texts]; What the Midianite daughters do after Moses helps them [divergence between the texts]; Moses helps the women at the water of Midian [divergence between the texts]; Moses' father-in-law in Midian [divergence between the texts]; and 15 more.

Only in Pharaoh's oppression and the infant Moses on the water: Moses' mother's heart becomes empty and she nearly discloses him, but God steadies her heart; God wills to favor the oppressed and make them leaders (aʾimma) and inheritors; Pharaoh exalted himself and divided the land's people into factions, oppressing one group; The oppressor slaughters the sons and lets the women live; Why Pharaoh oppresses Israel [divergence between the texts]; Hāmān appears as Pharaoh's minister and partner; Infant refuses other wet nurses; Mother receives divine instruction about the infant; Foster parent says: perhaps he will benefit us, or we will take him as a son; God addresses the hero with 'Fear not' in a vision; Ruler orders the killing of male infants; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

finding: Who decides that Moses be put on the water

units.title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry
Pharaoh's oppression and the infant Moses on the water

matches.label: Who decides that Moses be put on the water
matches.note: Who decides to put the child on the water: Exodus has the mother, on her own, hide him three months and, when she can hide him no longer (wə-lōʾ yākhlâ ʿôd haṣṣəfînô), make a papyrus basket sealed with pitch. In the Quran God inspires her (awḥaynā ilā ummi Mūsā): nurse him, cast him into the river when you fear, and 'we will return him to you and make him one of the messengers'. The rescue is announced in advance.

passages.text: וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֹתוֹ֙ כִּי ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַֽתִּצְפְּנֵ֖הוּ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יְרָחִֽים
וְלֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר
وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

matches.label: Infant placed in a container and set on the water
matches.note: fa-alqīhi fī l-yammi ~ wat-tāśem bas-sûf ʿal śəfat hay-yəʾōr: Exodus places him carefully among the reeds at the edge of the Nile (yəʾōr), in a basket (tēvat gōmeʾ) with bitumen and pitch; the Quran says 'cast him into the yamm', with no vessel in this passage, using the word that elsewhere names the sea where Pharaoh drowns.

passages.text: וְלֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר
وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

matches.label: Infant adopted by a royal woman
matches.note: Who finds and adopts him: Pharaoh's daughter (bat Parʿōh), bathing, sees the basket, has pity on the crying child, recognizes him as Hebrew (mī-yaldê hā-ʿIvrîm zeh) and later names him. In the Quran Pharaoh's household picks him up (iltaqaṭahu ālu Firʿawn), and Pharaoh's wife (imraʾat Firʿawn) pleads with Pharaoh: qurratu ʿaynin lī wa-laka lā taqtulūhu ʿasā an yanfaʿanā aw nattakhidhahu waladan. Daughter becomes wife, pity becomes intercession, and the Quran adds the divine irony 'so that he would be an enemy and a grief to them' (28:8).

passages.text: וַתֵּ֤רֶד בַּת פַּרְעֹה֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ עַל הַיְאֹ֔ר וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֥יהָ הֹלְכֹ֖ת עַל יַ֣ד הַיְאֹ֑ר וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֶת הַתֵּבָה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַסּ֔וּף וַתִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֶת אֲמָתָ֖הּ וַתִּקָּחֶֽהָ
וַתִּפְתַּח֙ וַתִּרְאֵ֣הוּ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וְהִנֵּה נַ֖עַר בֹּכֶ֑ה וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִיַּלְדֵ֥י הָֽעִבְרִ֖ים זֶֽה
וַיִגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֨הוּ֙ לְבַת פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מִן הַמַּ֖יִם מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ
فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ
وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّى وَلَكَ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

matches.label: Sister offers to find a nurse
matches.note: The sister's offer: Exodus has hăʾēlēkh wə-qārāʾtî lākh ʾiššâ mêneqet min hā-ʿIvriyyōt on her own initiative; the Quran first has God forbid the other wet-nurses to him (wa-ḥarramnā ʿalayhi l-marāḍiʿa min qablu), then the sister offers a household that will rear him. cf. b. Sotah 12b (Moses refuses Egyptian breasts), outside the HB.

passages.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲחֹתוֹ֮ אֶל בַּת פַּרְעֹה֒ הַאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְקָרָ֤אתִי לָךְ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה מֵינֶ֔קֶת מִ֖ן הָעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת וְתֵינִ֥ק לָ֖ךְ אֶת הַיָּֽלֶד
وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ

matches.label: Infant returned to his own mother to nurse
matches.note: Why the child goes back to his mother: Exodus has a paid arrangement with the princess, hêlîkhî ʾet hay-yeled haz-zeh wə-hênîqihû lî wa-ʾănî ʾettēn ʾet śəkhārēkh; the Quran has God keeping his promise, fa-radadnāhu ilā ummihi kay taqarra ʿaynuhā wa-lā taḥzana wa-li-taʿlama anna waʿda llāhi ḥaqqun. The Quran omits the naming and its etymology (Exod 2:10).

passages.text: וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה הֵילִ֜יכִי אֶת הַיֶּ֤לֶד הַזֶּה֙ וְהֵינִקִ֣הוּ לִ֔י וַאֲנִ֖י אֶתֵּ֣ן אֶת שְׂכָרֵ֑ךְ וַתִּקַּ֧ח הָאִשָּׁ֛ה הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַתְּנִיקֵֽהוּ
فَرَدَدْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

matches.label: Infant's sister watches over him
matches.note: qālat li-ukhtihi quṣṣīhi fa-baṣurat bihi ʿan junubin wa-hum lā yashʿurūna ~ wat-tētaṣṣav ʾăḥōtô mē-rāḥōq lə-dēʿâ mah yyēʿāśeh lô: the sister watches from a distance. In the Quran the mother sends her.

passages.text: וַתֵּתַצַּ֥ב אֲחֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק לְדֵעָ֕ה מַה יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה לֽוֹ
وَقَالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبٍ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

passages.text: וַתֵּ֤רֶד בַּת פַּרְעֹה֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ עַל הַיְאֹ֔ר וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֥יהָ הֹלְכֹ֖ת עַל יַ֣ד הַיְאֹ֑ר וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֶת הַתֵּבָה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַסּ֔וּף וַתִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֶת אֲמָתָ֖הּ וַתִּקָּחֶֽהָ

summary: 11 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: People fear to hear God directly and ask the prophet to mediate (weight 6.3); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property (weight 5.8); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8); No other gods before YHWH (weight 5.8); Prohibition of carved images or likenesses of anything for worship (weight 5.6); Sabbath rest on the seventh day for all, including servants, animals and strangers (weight 5.6); God visits the fathers' sin on the third and fourth generation, but keeps steadfast love for thousands (weight 5.6); The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) (weight 5.4); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.3); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness (weight 5.1). Pair score 62.2.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; Do not take God's name in vain; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; and 3 more.

Only in The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb: The covenant is made with those alive today, not only with the fathers; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; Mountain burns with fire to the heart of heaven amid darkness and cloud; The people answer as one: all that YHWH has spoken we will do [response between the texts]; Who was present at the revelation on the mountain, and who knows it only by report [contrast between the texts]; God heard as a voice out of fire with no visible form; The people's answer to the covenant ('we hear ...') [response between the texts]; Sabbath grounded in the memory of slavery in Egypt; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left; God gives stone tablets he himself has written.

לֹ֖א תִּנְאָֽף

sides.note: The same sequence: no other god, no killing, no adultery, no false witness: lā yadʿūna maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhara wa-lā yaqtulūna n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi wa-lā yaznūna ... lā yashhadūna z-zūra ~ lōʾ yihyeh ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāf ... lōʾ taʿăneh və-rēʿăkā ʿēd šāqer. Changes: the absolute lōʾ tirṣāḥ gets an exception ('except by right', illā bi-l-ḥaqq); theft is left out; the commands become a description of the righteous (alladhīna lā ...), followed by doubled punishment and an exception for those who repent (25:69-70).

matches.label: No other gods before YHWH
matches.note: lōʾ yihyeh-ləkā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ʿal-pānāy; lā tajʿal maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhar: same first commandment ('other gods' / 'another god'). The frame changes: Exod opens with the exodus, ʾăšer hôṣēʾtîkā mēʾereṣ miṣrayim; Q frames the code with the command at both ends (17:22, 17:39) and with no history of Israel, wa-qaḍā rabbuka. Q's code also has no Sabbath, no images clause and no coveting.

passages.text: אָֽנֹכִ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר הוֹצֵאתִ֛יךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים
לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ
لَّا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَّخْذُولًا

وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا
ذَٰلِكَ مِمَّآ أَوْحَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ رَبُّكَ مِنَ ٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتُلْقَىٰ فِى جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومًا مَّدْحُورًا

matches.label: Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life
matches.note: kabbēd ʾet-ʾābîkā wəʾet-ʾimmekā ləmaʿan yaʾărikûn yāmêkā; wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan immā yablughanna ʿindaka l-kibara ... fa-lā taqul lahumā uffin ... wa-qul rabbi rḥamhumā ka-mā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā. Q drops the promise of long life and puts in its place care for parents in old age and a prayer for them. Duty to parents comes second, right after God, in both.

passages.text: כַּבֵּ֥ד אֶת אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת אִמֶּ֑ךָ לְמַ֨עַן֙ יַאֲרִכ֣וּן יָמֶ֔יךָ עַ֚ל הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ

وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا
وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِى صَغِيرًا

matches.label: Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right
matches.note: lōʾ tirṣāḥ, unqualified; wa-lā taqtulu n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqq: Q adds 'except by right' and gives the victim's walī authority, fa-lā yusrif fī l-qatl, folding the blood-avenger law into the commandment.

passages.text: לֹ֖א תִּרְצָֽח
وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَمَن قُتِلَ مَظْلُومًا فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِۦ سُلْطَٰنًا فَلَا يُسْرِف فِّى ٱلْقَتْلِ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مَنصُورًا

matches.note: lōʾ tinʾāp; wa-lā taqrabū z-zinā innahu kāna fāḥishatan: Q forbids even approaching it, and its zinā covers any illicit intercourse, not only with a married woman.

title: Covenant Code - homicide, injury and the goring ox ↔ Retaliation and bequests
summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A negligent owner may pay a ransom for his life (weight 6.3); Retaliation (talion) for killing or injury [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth (lex talionis) (weight 5.4). Pair score 17.7.

Only in Covenant Code - homicide, injury and the goring ox: An animal that kills a person is stoned and its flesh not eaten; Men fighting strike a pregnant woman and she miscarries; One who injures another pays for his lost time and his healing; Whoever strikes a man so that he dies shall be put to death; A master who beats his slave to death is punished, unless the slave survives a day or two; Laws of the goring ox and the warned owner; A slave whose eye or tooth the master destroys goes free; Striking or cursing father or mother is a capital crime; The owner of an uncovered pit pays for an animal that falls in; A deliberate murderer is taken even from God's altar; Whether one who takes refuge at the sanctuary is safe [contrast between the texts]; A place of refuge for one who kills unintentionally; and 7 more.

Only in Retaliation and bequests: Kin of the slain may pardon and accept compensation (diya) instead of retaliation, a lightening from God; 'In retaliation there is life for you'; Retaliation (qisas) for the slain: free for free, slave for slave, female for female; Bequest (wasiyya) to parents and kin prescribed for one who leaves wealth; altering it is a sin; Whether payment may substitute for a life [contrast between the texts].

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Who must make pilgrimage to the sanctuary, and how often [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Do not invoke the names of other gods (weight 6.3); Three annual pilgrimage festivals when every male appears before God (weight 5.3). Pair score 17.9.

Only in Covenant Code - justice, enemy's animal, sabbatical year, festivals: Return your enemy's stray animal and help his overloaded donkey; Neither favor nor pervert justice for the poor in his lawsuit; Whoever commits a sin and casts it on an innocent bears slander and manifest sin; God does not forbid kindness and justice toward those who did not fight you over religion or expel you; Do not offer sacrificial blood with leavened bread; fat not left until morning; No one shall appear before God empty-handed; Do not oppress the stranger, for you were strangers in Egypt; The land lies fallow in the seventh year for the poor and wild animals; Let not hatred of a people move you to injustice; be just; Prohibition of boiling a kid in its mother's milk; Do not spread false reports or follow the majority to do wrong in court; How often and when pilgrimage is made [divergence between the texts]; and 4 more.

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts]; A place recognized as the house of God and gate of heaven; and 4 more.

Exodus says plainly that the elders saw God: wa-yyirʾû ʾēṯ ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl wə-ṯaḥaṯ raḡlâw kə-maʿăśēh liḇnaṯ has-sappîr ... wa-yyeḥĕzû ʾeṯ hā-ʾĕlōhîm wa-yyōʾḵəlû wa-yyištû. The Quran leaves the object unnamed: mā kadhaba l-fuʾādu mā raʾā; wa-la-qad raʾāhu nazlatan ukhrā (he saw him at another descent), and the exegetes dispute whether 'him' is God or Gabriel. Exodus' open sight of God has no plain counterpart in the Quran.

title: Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days ↔ Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God sends down his sakina (tranquility, cf. shekhinah) on the prophet and believers (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days: The cloud covers the mountain six days and God calls on the seventh; God's glory appears as a devouring fire; Joshua serves as Moses' attendant; Aaron and Hur left in charge while Moses is on the mountain; Moses leaves a deputy (Aaron, with or without Hur) with the people while he is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; Moses' set period on the mountain is forty (days and nights, or nights) [divergence between the texts]; A prophet spends forty days and forty nights in a set period; God gives stone tablets he himself has written.

Only in Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya: People of the Book who do not follow the true religion are fought until they pay the jizya, subdued; Polytheists are impure (najas) and may not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year; No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter the sanctuary; Gatekeepers stationed so that no one unclean enters the temple; Those counted impure are kept out of the sanctuary [divergence between the texts]; A large army must not claim the victory for itself [divergence between the texts]; City accepting peace becomes forced labor; one resisting has its males killed; The believers' pride in their great numbers avails nothing and the earth grows narrow for them (Hunayn); God supports the prophet with hosts (junud) the believers did not see; God reinforces the believers in battle with a thousand (or more) angels.

passages.text: (25:31) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מְנֹרַ֖ת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה תֵּעָשֶׂ֤ה הַמְּנוֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יִהְיֽוּ (25:32) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (25:33) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בַּקָּנֶ֥ה הָאֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (25:34) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (25:35) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (25:36) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה יִהְי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (25:37) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱלָה֙ אֶת נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔יהָ וְהֵאִ֖יר עַל עֵ֥בֶר פָּנֶֽיהָ (25:38) וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (25:39) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

passages.text: (37:17) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַמְּנֹרָ֖ה זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה עָשָׂ֤ה אֶת הַמְּנֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה הָיֽוּ (37:18) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (37:19) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (37:20) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁ֨קָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (37:21) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּֽחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנָּה (37:22) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה הָי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:23) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:24) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר עָשָׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל כֵּלֶֽיהָ

passages.text: (25:10) וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֲר֖וֹן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:11) וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתוֹ֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ תְּצַפֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ עָלָ֛יו זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:12) וְיָצַ֣קְתָּ לּ֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב וְנָ֣תַתָּ֔ה עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּעֹ֔ת עַל צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית (25:13) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בַדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב (25:14) וְהֵֽבֵאתָ֤ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֥את אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן בָּהֶֽם (25:15) בְּטַבְּעֹת֙ הָאָרֹ֔ן יִהְי֖וּ הַבַּדִּ֑ים לֹ֥א יָסֻ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ (25:16) וְנָתַתָּ֖ אֶל הָאָרֹ֑ן אֵ֚ת הָעֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ

(37:1) וַיַּ֧עַשׂ בְּצַלְאֵ֛ל אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (37:2) וַיְצַפֵּ֛הוּ זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר מִבַּ֣יִת וּמִח֑וּץ וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (37:3) וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּע֔וֹת עַל צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית (37:4) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בַּדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב (37:5) וַיָּבֵ֤א אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הָאָרֹֽן
וַיַּ֧עַשׂ בְּצַלְאֵ֛ל אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ

Only in Contribution for the sanctuary; ark, cover, table and lampstand: A cult object is hammered from a single piece of gold; A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark; List of precious materials for the sanctuary: metals, dyed yarns, linen, skins, wood, oil, spices, gems; God's voice speaks to Moses from above the ark cover between the two cherubim; The ark's carrying poles must never be removed; God will dwell in the midst of the people in a sanctuary; Exact dimensions in cubits are given for a sacred object of the sanctuary; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); Materials for the sanctuary come from the free-will gifts of all whose heart moves them; A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups; A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God; The tablets of the testimony are placed inside the ark; and 2 more.

Only in Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath): The ark (tabut) returns, carried by angels, containing tranquility (sakina) and relics left by the family of Moses and Aaron; David kills Jalut (Goliath) and is given kingship and wisdom; Were it not for God checking people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted; 'How many a small band has overcome a large one by God's leave'; God chose the king and increased him in knowledge and stature, though he lacked wealth; The people object that the chosen king has no wealth and they have more right to kingship; Before battle the army is tested at a river: whoever drinks is not with the leader, except a handful scooped by hand; What the ark contains [contrast between the texts]; David kills the Philistine giant [divergence between the texts]; A giant taunts Israel and is killed by a hero; A jar of manna preserved before the testimony for future generations; Objection raised against the newly chosen king [divergence between the texts]; and 9 more.

title: Tabernacle curtains, frames and veil ↔ Bezalel appointed; too many gifts; making of the curtains and frames
summary: 8 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A middle bar runs through the frames from end to end (weight 6.7); Eleven goat-hair curtains form the tent over the tabernacle (weight 6.7); Outer coverings of red-dyed ram skins and tahash skins (weight 6.7); Tabernacle walls of acacia frames set in silver sockets (weight 6.7); Curtains joined by fifty loops and fifty clasps (weight 6.7); An embroidered screen at the entrance of the tent or court (weight 6.7); A veil (parokhet) divides the holy place from the holy of holies (weight 6.3); Tabernacle curtains or veil woven with cherubim (weight 6.3). Pair score 52.7.

Only in Tabernacle curtains, frames and veil: The lampstand stands on the south side and the table on the north; The innermost room, the holy of holies, holds the ark; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

Only in Bezalel appointed; too many gifts; making of the curtains and frames: God gives the master craftsmen the ability to teach others; The people bring more than enough and must be told to stop giving; God calls a master craftsman by name for the sacred work; A second craftsman from the tribe of Dan assists the master craftsman; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; God fills craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom for sacred work.

passages.text: (26:15) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּ֖ים עֹמְדִֽים (26:16) עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ וְאַמָּה֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (26:17) שְׁתֵּ֣י יָד֗וֹת לַקֶּ֨רֶשׁ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד מְשֻׁלָּבֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל אֲחֹתָ֑הּ כֵּ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל קַרְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן (26:18) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֶשְׂרִ֣ים קֶ֔רֶשׁ לִפְאַ֖ת נֶ֥גְבָּה תֵימָֽנָה (26:19) וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אַדְנֵי כֶ֔סֶף תַּעֲשֶׂ֕ה תַּ֖חַת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ שְׁנֵ֨י אֲדָנִ֜ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֤רֶשׁ הָאֶחָד֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י יְדֹתָ֔יו וּשְׁנֵ֧י אֲדָנִ֛ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י יְדֹתָֽיו (26:20) וּלְצֶ֧לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית לִפְאַ֣ת צָפ֑וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֖ים קָֽרֶשׁ (26:21) וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּ֑סֶף שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (26:22) וּֽלְיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יָ֑מָּה תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שִׁשָּׁ֥ה קְרָשִֽׁים (26:23) וּשְׁנֵ֤י קְרָשִׁים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לִמְקֻצְעֹ֖ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן בַּיַּרְכָתָֽיִם (26:24) וְיִֽהְי֣וּ תֹֽאֲמִים֮ מִלְּמַטָּה֒ וְיַחְדָּ֗ו יִהְי֤וּ תַמִּים֙ עַל רֹאשׁ֔וֹ אֶל הַטַּבַּ֖עַת הָאֶחָ֑ת כֵּ֚ן יִהְיֶ֣ה לִשְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם לִשְׁנֵ֥י הַמִּקְצֹעֹ֖ת יִהְיֽוּ (26:25) וְהָיוּ֙ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה קְרָשִׁ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אֲדָנִ֑ים שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד

passages.text: (28:6) וְעָשׂ֖וּ אֶת הָאֵפֹ֑ד זָ֠הָב תְּכֵ֨לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֜ן תּוֹלַ֧עַת שָׁנִ֛י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מָשְׁזָ֖ר מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵֽׁב (28:7) שְׁתֵּ֧י כְתֵפֹ֣ת חֹֽבְרֹ֗ת יִֽהְיֶה לּ֛וֹ אֶל שְׁנֵ֥י קְצוֹתָ֖יו וְחֻבָּֽר (28:8) וְחֵ֤שֶׁב אֲפֻדָּתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ מִמֶּ֣נּוּ יִהְיֶ֑ה זָהָ֗ב תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מָשְׁזָֽר (28:9) וְלָ֣קַחְתָּ֔ אֶת שְׁתֵּ֖י אַבְנֵי שֹׁ֑הַם וּפִתַּחְתָּ֣ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם שְׁמ֖וֹת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (28:10) שִׁשָּׁה֙ מִשְּׁמֹתָ֔ם עַ֖ל הָאֶ֣בֶן הָאֶחָ֑ת וְאֶת שְׁמ֞וֹת הַשִּׁשָּׁ֧ה הַנּוֹתָרִ֛ים עַל הָאֶ֥בֶן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית כְּתוֹלְדֹתָֽם (28:11) מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה חָרַשׁ֮ אֶבֶן֒ פִּתּוּחֵ֣י חֹתָ֗ם תְּפַתַּח֙ אֶת שְׁתֵּ֣י הָאֲבָנִ֔ים עַל שְׁמֹ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מֻסַבֹּ֛ת מִשְׁבְּצ֥וֹת זָהָ֖ב תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם (28:12) וְשַׂמְתָּ֞ אֶת שְׁתֵּ֣י הָאֲבָנִ֗ים עַ֚ל כִּתְפֹ֣ת הָֽאֵפֹ֔ד אַבְנֵ֥י זִכָּרֹ֖ן לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְנָשָׂא֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן אֶת שְׁמוֹתָ֜ם לִפְנֵ֧י יְהוָ֛ה עַל שְׁתֵּ֥י כְתֵפָ֖יו לְזִכָּרֹֽן (28:13) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מִשְׁבְּצֹ֖ת זָהָֽב (28:14) וּשְׁתֵּ֤י שַׁרְשְׁרֹת֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִגְבָּלֹ֛ת תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה עֲבֹ֑ת וְנָתַתָּ֛ה אֶת שַׁרְשְׁרֹ֥ת הָעֲבֹתֹ֖ת עַל הַֽמִּשְׁבְּצֹֽת

(39:2) וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אֶת הָאֵפֹ֑ד זָהָ֗ב תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מָשְׁזָֽר (39:3) וַֽיְרַקְּע֞וּ אֶת פַּחֵ֣י הַזָּהָב֮ וְקִצֵּ֣ץ פְּתִילִם֒ לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת בְּת֤וֹךְ הַתְּכֵ֨לֶת֙ וּבְת֣וֹךְ הָֽאַרְגָּמָ֔ן וּבְת֛וֹךְ תּוֹלַ֥עַת הַשָּׁנִ֖י וּבְת֣וֹךְ הַשֵּׁ֑שׁ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה חֹשֵֽׁב (39:4) כְּתֵפֹ֥ת עָֽשׂוּ ל֖וֹ חֹבְרֹ֑ת עַל שְׁנֵ֥י קצוותו קְצוֹתָ֖יו חֻבָּֽר (39:5) וְחֵ֨שֶׁב אֲפֻדָּת֜וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֗יו מִמֶּ֣נּוּ הוּא֮ כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ֒ זָהָ֗ב תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֑ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת מֹשֶֽׁה

passages.text: (28:15) וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ חֹ֤שֶׁן מִשְׁפָּט֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה חֹשֵׁ֔ב כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה אֵפֹ֖ד תַּעֲשֶׂ֑נּוּ זָ֠הָב תְּכֵ֨לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֜ן וְתוֹלַ֧עַת שָׁנִ֛י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מָשְׁזָ֖ר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתֽוֹ (28:16) רָב֥וּעַ יִֽהְיֶ֖ה כָּפ֑וּל זֶ֥רֶת אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְזֶ֥רֶת רָחְבּֽוֹ (28:17) וּמִלֵּאתָ֥ בוֹ֙ מִלֻּ֣אַת אֶ֔בֶן אַרְבָּעָ֖ה טוּרִ֣ים אָ֑בֶן ט֗וּר אֹ֤דֶם פִּטְדָה֙ וּבָרֶ֔קֶת הַטּ֖וּר הָאֶחָֽד (28:18) וְהַטּ֖וּר הַשֵּׁנִ֑י נֹ֥פֶךְ סַפִּ֖יר וְיָהֲלֹֽם (28:19) וְהַטּ֖וּר הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י לֶ֥שֶׁם שְׁב֖וֹ וְאַחְלָֽמָה (28:20) וְהַטּוּר֙ הָרְבִיעִ֔י תַּרְשִׁ֥ישׁ וְשֹׁ֖הַם וְיָשְׁפֵ֑ה מְשֻׁבָּצִ֥ים זָהָ֛ב יִהְי֖וּ בְּמִלּוּאֹתָֽם (28:21) וְ֠הָאֲבָנִים תִּֽהְיֶ֜יןָ עַל שְׁמֹ֧ת בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה עַל שְׁמֹתָ֑ם פִּתּוּחֵ֤י חוֹתָם֙ אִ֣ישׁ עַל שְׁמ֔וֹ תִּֽהְיֶ֕יןָ לִשְׁנֵ֥י עָשָׂ֖ר שָֽׁבֶט

title: Ordination of the priests ↔ Moses ordains Aaron and his sons
summary: 10 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Ordination of priests lasts seven days (weight 6.7); Blood and anointing oil are sprinkled on the priests and their garments (weight 6.7); Anointing oil is poured on the head of the priest (weight 6.7); Portions are waved before God as a wave offering (weight 6.3); Sacred meat left over until morning is burned (weight 6.3); Blood is daubed on the right earlobe, thumb and big toe (weight 6.3); Priests are washed with water at the entrance before ordination (weight 6.3); Blood is put on the horns of the altar with the finger and poured at its base (weight 5.8); The flesh, skin and dung of the sin offering are burned outside the camp (weight 5.8); The offerer lays his hand on the head of the animal (weight 5.8). Pair score 62.5.

Only in Ordination of the priests: A basket of unleavened bread, oiled cakes and wafers is offered; An outsider may not eat holy food; The high priest's vestments pass to his successor, who wears them seven days; The breast and the right thigh are the priests' portion; Sacrificial animals must be without blemish; Whatever touches the most holy altar or holy things becomes holy; An offering by fire is a pleasing odor to God; The fat, the two kidneys and the lobe of the liver are burned on the altar; The fat tail of the sheep is offered.

Only in Moses ordains Aaron and his sons: Moses himself performs the priestly rites at the ordination; The whole congregation is assembled at the tent entrance to witness a rite; Anointing makes the tent and its furnishings holy; The refrain 'as YHWH commanded Moses' recurs in a sevenfold pattern; The ephod, a woven priestly garment with shoulder pieces; Urim and Thummim placed in the breastpiece for divine decision; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; A gold plate engraved 'Holy to YHWH' on the priest's forehead; A ritual action is performed seven times.
