title: The burning bush and the divine name ↔ Moses, Ishmael and Idris remembered; the later generation that neglected prayer (Surah 19:51-65)
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy) [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in Moses, Ishmael and Idris remembered; the later generation that neglected prayer (Surah 19:51-65): The angels say 'We descend only by your Lord's command'; God has no namesake or equal (samiyy); Ishmael was true to his promise and enjoined prayer and alms on his family; When the Merciful's verses are recited the prophets fall prostrate and weeping; In paradise the blessed receive their provision morning and evening; God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds; A prophet named Idrīs is mentioned among the righteous; God raised Idris to a high place; After the prophets came a generation that neglected prayer and followed lusts; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy); The covenant appointment is at the right (ayman) side of the Mount (al-Ṭūr); An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him [divergence between the texts]; and 5 more.

summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The call comes in the holy valley named Ṭuwā [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Hero told to remove his sandals because the place is holy ground (weight 6.3); A shepherd tending flocks comes to the mountain of God and is called (weight 6.3); God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed (weight 6.0). Pair score 31.5.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

Only in Moses at the fire in the holy valley Tuwa: The Hour is coming; God almost keeps it hidden so each soul is repaid for its striving; Prophet prays for his chest to be expanded and the knot of his tongue untied; Asked what is in his hand, the prophet lists his staff's uses: leaning, beating down leaves for sheep, other needs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; The call comes in the holy valley named Ṭuwā; Asked what is in his hand, the prophet lists his staff's uses: leaning, beating down leaves for sheep, other needs [divergence between the texts]; Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' [divergence between the texts]; Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him; Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign; and 3 more.

title: The burning bush and the divine name ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 3 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: What Moses asks Pharaoh to allow [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh (weight 6.7); The departing slaves ask their neighbors for silver, gold and clothing and so plunder their oppressors (weight 5.8); God identifies himself as God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (weight 5.6). Pair score 31.4.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Formulaic list of the Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Perizzite, Hivite and Jebusite; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy) [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; How the sea was split for the crossing [divergence between the texts]; and 38 more.

matches.note: The divine title before Pharaoh: YHWH ʾĕlōhê hā-ʿivriyyîm niqrâ ʿālênû (Exod 3:18, also 5:3) ~ innā rasūlu rabbi l-ʿālamīna, and when Pharaoh asks 'and what is the Lord of the worlds?', Moses answers rabbu s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi wa-mā baynahumā ... rabbu l-mashriqi wa-l-maghribi. matches.label: Why Moses approaches the fire
matches.note: Why Moses goes to the fire: Exodus has him alone with Jethro's flock at Horeb, turning aside to see the great sight (ʾāsurâ nāʾ wə-ʾerʾeh ʾet ham-marʾeh hag-gādōl haz-zeh); the Quran has him traveling with his family (qāla Mūsā li-ahlihi), going to bring back news or a burning brand 'that you may warm yourselves'. The Quran names neither flock, mountain nor Jethro.

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה אָסֻֽרָה נָּ֣א וְאֶרְאֶ֔ה אֶת הַמַּרְאֶ֥ה הַגָּדֹ֖ל הַזֶּ֑ה מַדּ֖וּעַ לֹא יִבְעַ֥ר הַסְּנֶֽה

matches.label: How God names himself to Moses from the fire
matches.note: God's self-identification from the fire: Exodus has ʾānōkhî ʾĕlōhê ʾāvîkā ʾĕlōhê ʾAvrāhām ʾĕlōhê Yiṣḥāq wē-ʾlōhê Yaʿăqōv, then ʾehyeh ʾăšer ʾehyeh; the Quran has yā Mūsā innahu ana llāhu l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu, preceded by subḥāna llāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīna. The God of the fathers becomes the Lord of the worlds, and the name-riddle becomes 'Allāh'. The Quran also leaves out the sandals and Moses hiding his face (Exod 3:5-6).

units.title: The burning bush and the divine name

matches.label: Where and how Moses comes to the place of his call
matches.note: Place and occasion of the call: Exodus has Moses shepherding Jethro's flock 'behind the wilderness' to Horeb, the mountain of God, a place of holy ground (ʾadmat qōdeš hûʾ), where he must take off his sandals. The Quran has Moses, after completing his term (qaḍā Mūsā l-ajala), traveling with his family, seeing fire on the side of the Mount (jānib aṭ-Ṭūr), and called from the right bank of the valley in 'the blessed spot' (al-buqʿa al-mubāraka). There are no flock and no sandals; the holy ground becomes a blessed spot.

title: The burning bush and the divine name ↔ Who revives rotten bones? Fire from the green tree; Be and it is
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God made fire for you from the green tree, from which you kindle (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in Who revives rotten bones? Fire from the green tree; Be and it is: The skeptic asks 'Who will give life to bones when they have rotted?'; the answer: he who produced them the first time; God asks 'Can these bones live?' and the prophet answers 'Lord God, you know'; The question whether dead bones can live again, and who asks it [divergence between the texts]; God created livestock and subjected them to people for riding, food, benefits and drink; Deity creates by spoken command (Let there be...); God originates creation and then repeats it (resurrection as re-creation); God creates by saying to a thing 'Be' and it is (kun fa-yakun).

title: The burning bush and the divine name ↔ Ha-Mim: the blessed night and the day of the smoke
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God identifies himself as God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in Ha-Mim: the blessed night and the day of the smoke: Opponents call the prophet 'one taught (by others), a madman' (mu'allam majnun); God lifts the punishment a little, but they revert; then comes 'the greatest assault' (al-batsha al-kubra); The Book was sent down on a blessed night in which every wise matter is decreed/distinguished (cf. the Night of Decree); Oath 'By the clear Book!' opening a surah; A day when the sky brings a visible smoke (dukhan) covering the people as a painful punishment; Smoke rises from the destroyed land like smoke of a kiln; God kills and makes alive, brings down to Sheol and raises up; 'There is none like you and no God beside you'; The king breaks his promise to release the people once a plague is lifted; Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga'); A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

matches.note: The God of the ancestors: YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾăḇōṯêḵem ʾĕlōhê ʾaḇrāhām ... zeh šəmî lə-ʿōlām vs. rabbukum wa-rabbu ābāʾikumu l-awwalīn. In Exodus the formula identifies the God of the fathers by name to Israel; in the Quran it tells Meccan polytheists that their own forefathers' Lord is the one God, against their appeal to ancestral custom.
